# What Is Usage-Based Pricing for AI?

Source: https://lowob.com/research/what-is-usage-based-pricing-for-ai/
Publisher: lowob (https://lowob.com)
Published: 2026-11-17
Function: Revenue

> Summary: Usage-based pricing for AI charges for the volume of work the AI does, measured in tokens, conversations, actions or credits, rather than per named user. It fits agents better than seat pricing, because one agent can do the work of several people. It also makes the bill harder to predict. Buyers should accept it only with caps, estimates and alerts, and with a clear idea of what one completed task costs.

*Figure: Where this piece sits in The Build Order: Gateway 0.*

## Key points

- Usage-based pricing bills for volume: tokens, conversations, actions or credits consumed, rather than seats.
- Salesforce moved Agentforce from $2 per conversation to Flex Credits in May 2025, at $500 per 100,000 credits, or $0.10 per action.
- Microsoft now uses Copilot Credits as a common currency for its usage-billed AI services, alongside fixed licences.
- Gartner, cited by Deloitte, expects at least 40% of enterprise SaaS spend to shift towards usage-, agent- or outcome-based pricing by 2030.
- Hybrid pricing, a platform fee or seats plus metered usage, is becoming the norm.

## What usage-based pricing means

Seat pricing charges per person with access. Usage-based pricing charges for what is consumed. For AI products the unit varies: raw tokens for model APIs, conversations for support agents, actions for agents that take steps, or credits, an abstract currency that converts each activity into a common count.

The shift is visible in the largest vendors. Salesforce launched Agentforce at $2 per conversation. In May 2025 it introduced Flex Credits: $500 per 100,000 credits, with each agent action consuming 20 credits, or $0.10. It kept a per-user option for employee-facing agents. Microsoft describes Copilot Credits as the unit of measure for its usage-based billing and a common currency across eligible services, available pay-as-you-go, in prepaid packs or through a pre-purchase plan.

| Unit | Example | Predictability for buyer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tokens | Model API calls | Low; depends on prompt length and model |
| Conversations | Early Agentforce pricing | Medium; conversation length varies |
| Actions | Agentforce Flex Credits | Medium; depends on how many steps an agent takes |
| Credits | Copilot Credits; many AI tools | Low to medium; conversion rates differ by feature |
| Seats plus allowance | Many business assistants | High; overage only above the allowance |

## Why it matters for a commercial team

Vendors are moving because agents break the link between users and value. Gartner warned in July 2026 that agentic AI "breaks the link between user growth and revenue growth" for many software vendors. If one agent does the follow-up work of five sellers, five seats undercharge for it. Usage pricing lets the bill follow the work.

For the buyer, the risk moves too. Under seats the vendor carries the cost of heavy users. Under usage the buyer does, and agents can be heavy users. An agent that retries, loops or takes twelve steps where four would do costs three times as much. Pricing also changes often. Metronome, a billing vendor that catalogued more than 50 AI pricing models in April 2026, found that hybrid models are now the norm, and that one coding tool had changed its pricing structure four times in under two years.

Adoption is broad among AI-native vendors. Deloitte cites a Maxio survey finding that 83% of AI-native SaaS companies offer usage-based pricing. Maxio sells billing software, so treat the figure as vendor research.

## How to evaluate a usage-based AI contract

The test is whether you can predict next month's bill to within a range you can defend to finance.

| Question to ask | Why it matters |
| --- | --- |
| What is the unit, and what triggers one? | "Action" and "conversation" are defined by the vendor |
| Can we set hard caps by team or agent? | Stops a looping agent becoming a budget incident |
| Do we get alerts before a threshold, within the month? | Renewal is too late to discover overspend |
| Is there an estimator using our own volumes? | Generic calculators assume the vendor's average |
| What does one completed task cost us? | The only number that compares vendors fairly |
| Can unused credits roll over, and do they expire? | Prepaid packs can turn into shelfware |

Work out cost per completed task before signing. Count the tasks a workflow completes in a month, such as follow-up drafts approved or briefs used in a meeting, and divide the expected bill by that count. Include the time people spend reviewing. Compare that figure with the seat price for the same cohort. Start with the people in one commercial workflow, and expand on evidence.

## lowob takeaways

- **Usage follows the work.** It suits agents better than seats, because one agent can replace several users' effort.
- **The risk moves to you.** Caps, estimates and in-month alerts are conditions of purchase, not extras.
- **Hybrid is the norm.** Expect a platform fee or seats plus metered usage.
- **Compare on cost per task.** Credits and actions are not comparable across vendors; completed tasks are.

## Common questions

### What is usage-based pricing for AI?

A pricing model that charges for the volume of AI work done, measured in tokens, conversations, actions or credits, rather than per named user.

### How much does Salesforce Agentforce cost per action?

Under Flex Credits, introduced in May 2025, each action uses 20 credits. Credits cost $500 per 100,000, which works out at $0.10 per action. Earlier pricing was $2 per conversation.

### What are AI credits?

A vendor-defined currency that converts different AI activities into one count for billing. Different features consume different numbers of credits, so a credit price alone does not tell you what a task costs.

### Is usage-based or seat-based pricing better for AI tools?

Seats suit tools a person uses daily, where their time is the value. Usage suits agents whose value scales with volume. Many contracts now combine the two.
